checks.claim: C1: q_sigma is legal with common support, q_avg is nonzero, and h_sigma>=U_avg>=0.
checks.reason: For u,sigma in [0,1], the kernel is at least 1 and positive almost everywhere. By continuity of psi(.,x), q_sigma(x)=0 holds exactly when psi(.,x) vanishes identically, which holds exactly when q_avg(x)=0. The positivity sets and supports therefore coincide. Differentiation under the integrable kernel gives smoothness. A positive Radon convolution preserves the order in both the Riesz and white cases.

checks.reason: Tilt Section 3 assumes only real psi, not separability. It bounds every spatial derivative, gives the time derivative through the kernel over temporal distances at most 1, and proves Lipschitz dependence into C_b^1 and uniform W1,infinity tails. Those are the facts the candidate uses: M, C_h, R_ext and frozen admissibility with zero constant part in local-flow (5.6).

Autonomy gives the semigroup law through uniqueness. The finite-horizon bound (5.2) depends only on the common W1,infinity bound. checks.reason: Since w_R=1 on [-R,R], which contains [-D,D], and h_sigma>=U_avg>=0, the form is at most A/R-m, which is at most -m/2 by R>=2A/m. Dividing by ||w_R||^2=RB gives eps=m/(2RB), independent of sigma. H_sigma>=-M is immediate. A>0 holds because chi is compact and equals 1 on [-1,1].

checks.claim: C2: The bottom is in the spectrum and is a discrete eigenvalue before conditional positivity is invoked; p_sigma is real, L2-normalized and pointwise strictly positive.
checks.reason: The order in lines 95-99 is correct: Rayleigh via T4.12 with n=1, spectrum, below essential 0, then T10.13. H2 gives C1, the ODE gives C2, and a zero of a nonnegative solution has zero derivative, so ODE uniqueness rules it out. Line 101 gives l<=lambda_sigma<=sqrt(M).

checks.claim: C2: Common max-min classes give level Lipschitz bounds, with E2 capped at 0 and multiplicity/infinite Riesz states allowed.
checks.reason: U(psi_1,...) in (4.37) is the same set for every sigma because the domain H2 (or form domain H1) is common. The form difference is at most D_(sigma,s), and this survives inf then sup. T4.12 counts multiplicity and sets later levels to the essential infimum. No eigenvector selection is used. E1<E2<=0 follows from simplicity plus isolation.

checks.claim: C2: Compactness gives Delta>0 and exact rate separation; no uniform gap is a premise.
checks.reason: E2-E1 is positive and continuous on [0,1]. Then lambda-mu=(E2-E1)/(lambda+mu) and lambda+mu<=2L_rate, with lambda>=l keeping the denominator positive. This gives d_rate=Delta/(2L_rate), and mu=0 is allowed.

checks.claim: C3: The energy, H2, sup and vanishing bounds at both infinities are uniform.
checks.reason: ||p'||^2=int h p^2-lambda^2<=M and ||p''||_2<=lambda^2+M<=2M. The inequality ||g||_inf^2<=2||g||_2||g'||_2, applied to p and p', plus H1 approximation gives uniform bounds and vanishing of p and p' at both ends.

checks.claim: C3: One common exterior R_ext and beta, with unbounded half-line comparison, give uniform p, p', p'' tails.
checks.reason: With beta=l/2 and h<=l^2/2 for |x|>=R_ext, one has p''>=(l^2/2)p>=beta^2 p. The difference w vanishes at R_ext and at infinity and satisfies w''-beta^2 w>=0, so it has no positive maximum. The boundary value is bounded by the uniform sup bound. The ODE gives the p'' tail, and integrating from infinity using p'->0 gives the p' tail with constant C/beta. No Agmon constant is used.

checks.claim: C3: The exact residual sign, gap inverse, positive overlap and H2/lambda continuity hold without assuming eigenfunction continuity.
checks.reason: H_s=H_sigma+h_sigma-h_s gives the residual [E1(sigma)-E1(s)+h_sigma-h_s]p_sigma, of norm at most 2D_(sigma,s). On the complement of p_s the spectrum of H_s-E1(s) is at least E2(s)-E1(s)>=Delta. With b>0, 2(1-b)<=2(1-b^2)=2||Q p_sigma||^2. In the subtracted ODE the coefficient of p_s has sup norm at most 2D_(sigma,s). Also |lambda_sigma-lambda_s|=|E1(sigma)-E1(s)|/(lambda_sigma+lambda_s)<=D_(sigma,s)/(2l).

checks.reason: Compact smooth and constant data have classical bounded-derivative solutions using bounded derivatives of h_sigma and kernel mass tau-u. With p''+h p=lambda^2 p, a''=lambda^2 a, so y=(a+a'/lambda)/2 has y'=lambda y. The dense extension uses bounded ell and P on the compact-plus-constant class. The eigenphase is identified by uniqueness. Both sides of (14) equal exp(lambda tau)e ell.
